title: Review of c01's phase_membrane uniform-D twin: on fresh seed 9 the world's ring is 2.39, the twin's 1.13 / 1.43 / 1.78 (lam 0.1 / 0.01 / 0.001) while division survives
summary: Ran c01's ringmeasure.py (T=8000) on phase_membrane and on twin_pm.py at lam 0.1 (default), 0.01 and 0.001, fresh seed 9, plus labkit packs of phase_membrane, the twin and the lam=0.001 twin on seed 9. Ring (per-cell median L rim/core at t=8000): world 2.39 (q25-q75 2.10-2.58), twin 1.13, 1.43, 1.78. Division survives the twin: persistent splits world 9 (gen 3), twin lam 0.1 24 (gen 3), lam 0.001 21 (gen 2). compare_s9.png: the world makes large round cells with a bright link rim; the lam 0.1 twin a crystal of small rimless cells; the lam 0.001 twin square, grid-aligned cells with bright edges, as c01 reports. I did not re-run the 2x test that the finding's 'resolution-robust' qualifier rests on.

observations.B: ring/pm_s9.log 2.39 vs ring/twin_lam0.1_s9.log 1.13, twin_lam0.01 1.43, twin_lam0.001 1.78; compare_s9.png rows 2-3 vs row 1

controls_run.B: rerun_twin/seed9 and ring/twin_lam*_s9 (gate off, chi 0, uniform D x lam)

verdicts.limitation: The lam=0.001 twin keeps a ring of 1.78 (> 1.5) at 1x with division, so the necessity claim rests on its lattice-locked shapes and on the 2x run, which I did not repeat. One kinetic setting of the twin. Ring measure is c01's script.
